messages:
From: Jenna Park <jenna@quantaflow.ai>

Subject: Kickoff: Dedicated pool + autoscale plan (Quantaflow)

Hi Lauren / Monica,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Quantaflow is excited to move forward with Redwood Dedicated for our inference workload. Before we lock dates, Rajesh asked me to get alignment on the explicit provisioning and autoscaling plan so our infra team can approve network access and budget.

High level we expect: 8 steady GPUs for core traffic (in us-west-2) with the ability to burst up to 20 GPUs for peak inference windows. Average infer size is ~120 tokens; concurrent requests vary 200-700 qps per shard (attached a weekly traffic sample).

Can you confirm:
- recommended base pool size vs burst config for the workload above
- autoscale policy suggestions (metrics & thresholds)
- expected warm-up / cold-start behavior when bursting to new GPUs
- what regional failover options we should provision now for disaster scenarios

We'd like to aim for a staged activation starting Oct 26 (PoC period) and full go-live Nov 9.

Attaching: quantaflow-expected-traffic.csv

Thanks,
Jenna Park
Head of SRE, Quantaflow

From: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Jenna Park <jenna@quantaflow.ai>
Cc: monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 11:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Kickoff: Dedicated pool + autoscale plan (Quantaflow)

Thanks Jenna — welcome aboard. Quick replies inline and an implementation cadence proposal below. Monica will handle the provisioning checklist and KMS/access items; I'll own the activation schedule and success criteria.

Inline:
- Base vs burst: Based on the attached traffic sample we recommend a starting reserved pool of 8 A100-equivalent GPUs with burst capacity configured to allow up to 20 GPUs in the same region. For sustained peaks we suggest converting 4 of the burst slots to reserved after the PoC (typical pattern we see).
- Autoscale policy: Start with CPU/GPU utilization + request queue length. Recommended thresholds: scale-up when avg GPU util > 65% for 60s OR request queue > 150 for 30s; scale-down when avg GPU util < 35% for 120s AND queue < 50. We'll provide a JSON policy you can drop into your console.
- Warm-up behavior: cold starts for new GPUs are typically 12–25s depending on model variant and quantization. We strongly recommend keeping a small warm standby (1–2 nodes) if sub-2s P95 latency is required; otherwise use prefix KV caching to reduce token generation on short prompts.
- Regional failover: Primary: us-west-2, Passive failover: us-east-1 with automated routing policy. Active-active is possible but will increase egress and cross-region replication complexity.

Implementation cadence (proposed):
1) Today–Oct 16: Security & networking checklist (Monica + Quantaflow NetOps)
2) Oct 19–23: Provision reserved pool + burst config; deploy sample model and run load tests
3) Oct 26–30: PoC window (gradual traffic ramp to 30%)
4) Nov 2–6: Cutover dry-run; confirm SLA metrics and tracing
5) Nov 9: Full go-live

I've attached the activation runbook (v1) — Monica, please add provisioning tickets and the KMS flow. Rishi, if you have any SLA or pricing exceptions to note, flag them here.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Senior Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

Hi all — Monica here with the provisioning checklist and a couple of netops notes.

Checklist (incoming to us from Quantaflow):
- VPC peering proposal (request subnet/RFC1918 ranges and any overlapping CIDR)
- Firewall egress rules for telemetry endpoints (we'll provide endpoints)
- KMS key ARN for model keys + customer-managed key option if required
- Service account emails for onboarding automation (we'll create service principal)

Technical notes:
- For the burst pool to scale quickly we need to enable our pre-warmed image option (adds ~6s faster warm-up vs bare boot). We'll enable that for the burst slots.
- Network egress: if you choose active-active across regions, expect cross-region sync events; we recommend passive failover unless you have strict multi-region latency requirements.

Action items for Quantaflow:
- Share the VPC CIDR and a contact for firewall rule approvals
- Confirm whether you want customer-managed KMS or Redwood-managed keys

I'll open the provisioning ticket today (RED-PRV-6732) and include the runbook. Karthik, can you propose autoscale gain/policy knobs for the JSON drop?

Thanks,
Monica Patel

Quick technical add from infra side — proposing the autoscale knobs we'll use in the PoC JSON. Drop-in recommendations:

- metric: gpu_utilization (moving avg 60s), queue_length (instant)
- scale_up: {"gpu_utilization": ">=65% for 60s", "queue_length": ">=150 for 30s"}
- scale_down: {"gpu_utilization": "<=35% for 120s", "queue_length": "<=50"}
- cooldown: 90s after any scale event to avoid flapping
- burst_granularity: add GPUs in increments of 2 to reduce overshoot
- prewarm_policy: enable for up to 8 burst nodes during known peak windows (you can schedule based on cron)

Operational note: we'll expose trace headers for customer telemetry so Quantaflow can correlate request IDs during PoC. Let's plan for a 2‑hour load test window during the PoC where Quantaflow sends production-like traffic to validate scale and latency.

I'll attach the sample JSON in the provisioning ticket (RED-PRV-6732).

-karthik
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
